drafts.angle: Tool comparisons are useful, but the real prospecting decision isn't which platform wins — it's whether your team has the fundamentals (targeting, messaging, domain hygiene) sorted before adding more tooling.

linkedin.content:
Comparison guides for sales tooling have their place. But here's what they rarely say out loud: a better tool won't fix a weak list or a message nobody wants to read.

The Instantly Blog published a solid breakdown of AI prospecting platforms — Instantly, Apollo, Clay, Lemlist — evaluated on deliverability, pricing, and team controls. Worth a read if you're in the market. https://instantly.ai/blog/best-ai-sales-prospecting-tools/

What we'd add: the teams that get real mileage from these tools usually have one thing in common. They've already done the slower work — defining a tight ICP, building a clean sending infrastructure, and writing copy that earns a reply. The platform becomes a multiplier at that point, not a fix.

If you're evaluating tooling and want to think through the outbound setup around it, feel free to reach out at https://salesmake.agency/contact.

instagram.content:
Better tools ≠ better results — not on their own.

The Instantly Blog dropped a detailed comparison of AI sales prospecting platforms (Instantly, Apollo, Clay, Lemlist) — useful reading if you're evaluating infrastructure.

But here's the thing we keep coming back to:
→ A sharper tool on a blurry ICP still misses
→ Deliverability features don't rescue flat copy
→ The platform is a multiplier, not a foundation

Sort the fundamentals first. Then let the tooling do its job.
